name: Tween
simple: A Tween is one ready-to-play smooth animation of an object's properties. You get one from `TweenService:Create()`, then you can Play, Pause or Cancel it, and listen for when it is Completed. Once made, its settings cannot be changed; make a new Tween if you need different goals.
analogy: A Tween is like a recorded TV show. TweenService records it, and the Tween is the remote control: play, pause, stop, and a light that tells you when the show is over.
whenToUse: Pause a moving platform with `:Pause()` and resume it later with `:Play()`
Do something after an animation ends using `Completed`
where: Server and client. You cannot use `Instance.new("Tween")`; you must make it with `game:GetService("TweenService"):Create(...)`.

terms.tween: Short for "in-between". A smooth change of a property from its current value to a goal value over time.
terms.read-only: You can look at the value, but you cannot change it.
terms.PlaybackState: Where the tween is in its life: `Begin` (made but never played), `Delayed` (waiting for its delay time), `Playing`, `Paused`, `Completed` (finished normally) or `Cancelled` (stopped early).
terms.event: Something that happens in the game that your code can listen for, like a doorbell. You `:Connect` a function to run when it rings.
terms.inherits: Gets features from a parent class. Tween gets Play, Pause, Cancel, PlaybackState and Completed from a class called TweenBase.
terms.TweenInfo: The settings that say how a tween moves: time, easing style, easing direction, repeat count, reverses, and delay.

examples.title: Play, pause and resume a moving platform
examples.code:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")

local platform = script.Parent
platform.Anchored = true

local info = TweenInfo.new(4, Enum.EasingStyle.Linear)
local tween = TweenService:Create(platform, info, {
    Position = platform.Position + Vector3.new(30, 0, 0),
})

tween:Play()
task.wait(2)        -- let it move for 2 seconds (about halfway)
tween:Pause()       -- freeze where it is
print(tween.PlaybackState) -- Enum.PlaybackState.Paused
task.wait(3)
tween:Play()        -- carries on from where it stopped

tween.Completed:Connect(function(state)
    print("Tween ended with state:", state) -- Enum.PlaybackState.Completed
end)
explain: We make a 4-second tween that slides the platform 30 studs along X.
After 2 seconds we pause it. Pausing keeps its progress.
Calling `Play` again continues from where it paused.
`Completed` tells us when it is finished and why (Completed or Cancelled).

gotchas: `Pause` keeps the progress; `Cancel` throws the progress away. After a Cancel, `Play` starts over and takes the full time again.
`Cancel` does NOT put the part back to where it started. It just stops it where it is.
`Pause` does not fire the `Completed` event, but `Cancel` does.
Calling `Play` on a tween that is already playing does nothing.
You cannot change a tween's goal or time after making it. Create a new tween instead.

Tween.Instance.simple: The object this tween is changing, like the Part or Frame you passed to `TweenService:Create()`. Read-only.
Tween.Instance.example:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local tween = TweenService:Create(workspace.Part, TweenInfo.new(1), {Transparency = 1})
print(tween.Instance.Name) -- Part

Tween.TweenInfo.simple: The TweenInfo settings this tween was made with: its time, easing style, easing direction, repeat count, reverses and delay. Read-only.
Tween.TweenInfo.example:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local tween = TweenService:Create(workspace.Part, TweenInfo.new(3), {Transparency = 1})
print(tween.TweenInfo.Time) -- 3 (seconds)
print(tween.TweenInfo.EasingStyle) -- Enum.EasingStyle.Quad (the default)

TweenBase.PlaybackState.simple: Tells you what the tween is doing right now: Begin, Delayed, Playing, Paused, Completed or Cancelled. Read-only; change it by calling Play, Pause or Cancel.
TweenBase.PlaybackState.example:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local tween = TweenService:Create(workspace.Part, TweenInfo.new(2), {Transparency = 1})
print(tween.PlaybackState) -- Enum.PlaybackState.Begin
tween:Play()
print(tween.PlaybackState) -- Enum.PlaybackState.Playing

TweenBase:Play.simple: Starts the tween, or continues it after a Pause. If it is already playing, nothing happens.
TweenBase:Play.example:
local TweenService = game:GetService("TweenService")
local tween = TweenService:Create(workspace.Part, TweenInfo.new(1), {Transparency = 1})
tween:Play() -- the part fades out over 1 second

TweenBase:Pause.simple: Freezes the tween where it is and remembers its progress, so `Play` continues from that spot. Does not fire `Completed`.
TweenBase:Pause.example:
tween:Play()
task.wait(0.5)
tween:Pause() -- freeze halfway
task.wait(2)
tween:Play()  -- continue from halfway
TweenBase:Pause.gotcha: Only a tween that is currently playing can be paused.

TweenBase:Cancel.simple: Stops the tween and forgets its progress. The object stays where it was when you cancelled; it does not jump back. If you `Play` again later, it takes the full time to reach the goal. Fires `Completed` with the state Cancelled.
TweenBase:Cancel.example:
tween:Play()
task.wait(1)
tween:Cancel() -- stop now; the part stays wherever it got to
TweenBase:Cancel.gotcha: Cancel does not undo the changes. If you want the part back at the start, set its property back yourself or tween it back.

TweenBase.Completed.simple: An event that fires when the tween finishes, or when it is cancelled. It tells you which one happened by giving you a PlaybackState (Completed or Cancelled). Pausing does not fire it.
TweenBase.Completed.example:
tween.Completed:Connect(function(playbackState)
    if playbackState == Enum.PlaybackState.Completed then
        print("Finished all the way!")
    end
end)
tween:Play()
